messages:
tara: FYI customer reported repeated SSE disconnects and partial outputs from the streaming API. They say streams drop after ~35s and clients see a truncated JSON payload. Escalating — can oncall look?

kevin-oncall: on it. do we have request id / customer id? also which endpoint?

tara: customer_id=acme-184, request id=rx-7c9d. endpoint: POST /v1/streams (SSE). Happening from both browser and server clients. They say auto-reconnect doesn't always resume from last-event-id, so duplicates or missing tokens.

samir: got logs for rx-7c9d: attach from edge. main error: "upstream prematurely closed connection" then "broken pipe". Looks like proxy idle timeout.

eng-sre-bot: alert: stream_disconnects spike 4x in last 2h for region us-west-2. top error tags: upstream_closed, client_reset, timeout.

liam: @kevin-oncall quick notes — common root causes: 1) HTTP idle timeouts on LB/nginx 2) proxies that buffer chunked responses and close them after threshold 3) app-level cancellation when request context times out 4) client-side parsers failing on partial token chunks.

kevin-oncall: can we repro internally? samir, can you share curl that reproduces?

samir: repro with curl:

```
# run from a machine with a valid API key
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=redwood/lite" \
  | sed -n '1,200p'
```

Observed output: server sends several SSE events, then a comment line `:\n` heartbeat, then suddenly connection resets and last event is incomplete JSON: `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"The quick brown f` 

liam: thanks — that partial token is exactly what happens when the TCP connection drops mid-chunk. For SSE we recommend server-side heartbeats (colon comments) at intervals < LB idle timeout to keep proxies from closing connection. Browsers' EventSource will auto-reconnect but the client needs to reassemble from last-event-id.

maria: product question — is it safe for us to add server-side comment pings by default? any perf or cost impact?

liam: minimal CPU/bytes. small comment like `:\n

` every 15s keeps most LBs happy. alternative: send a tiny SSE event `event: ping\ndata: {"t": 169...}

` — but comments are lower overhead and ignored by EventSource.

jessica: billing note — customers streaming long-lived connections increase egress/connection-minutes costs. if we change default heartbeat frequency we should call out billing impact in release notes.

kevin-oncall: immediate mitigation for acme-184: increase proxy timeouts and configure nginx `proxy_read_timeout` to 300s in front of runtime for that customer domain. also enable `tcp_nodelay` and OS keepalive on instance-level to detect broken sockets faster.

liam: long-term we should:
- send comment heartbeats every 15s for SSE streams
- include `retry: 5000` line in SSE stream header so clients backoff predictably
- emit `id:` events with monotonically increasing id so clients can resume at last-event-id
- add server-side token-level chunk markers (for clients that need exact reassembly) OR encourage newline-delimited JSON for streaming outputs

samir: copying suggested code snippet for heartbeat middleware (Go pseudocode):

```
// inside stream handler
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)
// write initial SSE headers
w.Write([]byte("retry: 5000\\n\\n"))
flusher.Flush()

ticker := time.NewTicker(15 * time.Second)
defer ticker.Stop()
for {
  select {
  case <-ticker.C:
    // send a comment ping so proxies count activity
    w.Write([]byte(":\\n\\n"))
    flusher.Flush()
  case <-ctx.Done():
    return
  }
}
```

liam: also add observability: increment `stream.heartbeat_sent`, track `stream.connection_duration_seconds`, `stream.bytes_sent`, and count `stream.disconnect_reason` tags.

maria: product follow-ups: we should add a short section in Streaming docs about keepalive, and a snippet for common proxies (nginx, aws alb, gcp lb). I'll draft.

kevin-oncall: ops checklist for this incident:
- [x] raised customer support incident (PID 4721)
- [x] temporary increase proxy_read_timeout for acme domain
- [x] deploy heartbeat middleware to canary runtime pool (low risk)
- [ ] monitor for dropped reconnects and duplicate tokens for 1h

samir: customer feedback — they had some clients using custom HTTP clients (Go net/http) with default Dialer keepalive disabled. recommend we add a client note: ensure TCP keepalive and disable aggressive HTTP client timeouts.

jessica: also saw billing spike because some clients aggressively reconnected in a tight loop after disconnects. recommend we document exponential backoff with jitter and set a default `retry` of 5s so browsers and clients don't hammer.

liam: FYI about Last-Event-ID: browsers automatically set `Last-Event-ID` header on reconnect only if event ids are present. So we must populate `id:` on each SSE message for reliable resume.

maria: thanks team. actionable plan: (1) docs + proxy best-practices section (maria) (2) heartbeat middleware roll to canary (liam) (3) telemetry to detect reconnect anomalies (kevin) (4) customer-facing guidance + billing note (jessica) (5) follow-up with acme-184 and confirm fixes (samir).

kevin-oncall: I'll watch the canary deploy. ping me if we see disconnects persist after 15m. :eyes:

samir: I emailed acme-184 support contact with repro steps and asked them to test with the curl command and confirm after canary.

eng-sre-bot: incident update: canary heartbeat deployed to runtime pool r-03 at 1763225660, metrics will be available in 120s.

kevin-oncall: closing this slack thread once we have 1h of stable telemetry or a customer confirmation. leaving it open for now.
